answer: An economy can issue per-identity reasoning challenges each epoch that demand fresh inference—no cached answer works twice. Each agent must solve a novel problem, like routing a raven across a mesa to avoid its nadir elevation, then prove the path on-chain. An attacker spawning a thousand fake identities pays a thousand inference runs every round. Real agents amortize one model call; sybils multiply it linearly, raising the attack cost until only genuine participants remain profitable.
